findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:731`: check_result calls msgspec.to_builtins (data(raw)) on the caller-supplied Valid value without any size bound first. The two-argument *_disposition wrappers pass any forged Completed(Valid(...)) through to it, so containers that share references expand exponentially. _nonready (data(prepared) on a forged OriginGap) and _typed_origin's data(raw) on non-object typed fields have the same problem.

   Failure scenario: Build l0=['x']*32, then l_{k+1}=[l_k]*32 up to l7. Call sufficiency_disposition(real_ready, Completed(Valid({'format':1,'kind':'sufficiency',...,'outcome':{'status':'groom','gaps':l7,...}}))). to_builtins tries to build about 32^8 nodes before strict convert can reject anything, ending in a hang or an uncaught MemoryError. A total projection should return HoldUnavailable('bad_output').
findings.disposition: Addressed: bounded occurrence/depth/string-byte prewalk runs before msgspec conversion, including normalized model and OriginGap paths. Shared and cyclic graphs are refused without expansion. Float and malformed Unicode remain owned by later profile/unsafe validation.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:585`: prepare's typed-request path wraps _typed_origin only in `except Fault`. A forged typed record (msgspec Struct __init__ does not validate types) raises AttributeError from _candidate/_text, or TypeError from to_builtins, out of prepare. The same exceptions escape egress() and the four-argument disposition().

   Failure scenario: prepare(SufficiencyRequest(..., candidate=Candidate(title=None, ...)), privacy) reaches `None.encode` in _text and raises AttributeError. prepare(IntakeRequest(..., open_tasks=(object(),)), privacy) makes to_builtins raise TypeError. Both should come back as InvalidHost or OriginGap, not raise; disposition('sufficiency', c.Ready(forged), None, privacy) crashes the same way.
findings.disposition: Addressed: malformed typed origin validation failures become InvalidHost or OriginGap; egress and the explicit four-argument projection cannot propagate those exceptions. Unsupported objects are refused before conversion.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/project.py:46`: `prepared.reason_code in HOST_CODES` (and line 142, `attempt.reason_code not in HOST_CODES`) does a set lookup on an unvalidated host token. An unhashable forged reason_code raises TypeError instead of mapping to invalid_host.

   Failure scenario: intake_disposition(c.HostFailed(['timeout']), None) raises TypeError: unhashable type 'list'. So does intake_disposition(real_ready, c.HostFailed({})). The D4 rule that unknown codes in supposedly typed host objects are invalid_host is broken by an exception.
findings.disposition: Addressed: both prepared and attempted HostFailed require an exact string code before set lookup; malformed/unhashable codes hold invalid_host.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:839`: egress validates through prepare(request, privacy) but then builds the DTO from the caller's original `request` (invocation.input, ask.effect/excludes/why/risks) instead of the validated copy in prepared.value. The output therefore shares mutable host objects, or list/dict subclasses, that were never what got checked.

   Failure scenario: A host prepares a request from a dict, so convert keeps raw['invocation']['input'] by reference, then calls egress(ready.value, p). The returned DTO's 'input' is that same caller-owned dict. Setting input['cmd']='/home/alice/.claude' afterwards changes the model payload with no re-check. A dict subclass whose __iter__ hides keys from _native would be serialized by whatever reads the real storage.
findings.disposition: Addressed: egress builds exclusively from the detached validated request returned by prepare. Host mutation cannot alter an already-returned DTO; untrusted container subclasses are refused.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:722`: check_result, the only result check the two-argument dispositions re-run, has no aggregate response bound. Only decode_result enforces the 32 KiB limit, on raw bytes. A forged normalized Valid can carry far more than D4's whole-response limit and still project successfully.

   Failure scenario: sufficiency_disposition(ready, Completed(Valid(SufficiencyJudgment(..., Groom(gaps=64 x 4096-byte details, ...))))) returns NeedsGrooming carrying about 256 KiB of model text. D4 says output that is valid item by item but over the whole-response limit is completed invalid/oversize, mapping to HoldUnavailable('bad_output').
findings.disposition: Addressed: normalized check_result enforces the whole canonical 32768-byte response bound before conversion and outcome validation. Whole oversized model data maps to bad_output, with zero partial grooming output.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/project.py:83`: The atomic overflow check sizes the reassessment using the current revision and request_id. D4 requires the mandatory Used reassessment to have a new revision (changed whenever judged input changes), and it may have a different request_id, so the budget does not reserve for those fields growing.

   Failure scenario: canonical(rebuilt) comes to exactly 131072 bytes at revision 99 with a 10-character request_id, so EnrichmentProposal is returned. The required reassessment at revision 100 with a fresh 36-character request_id is over 131072, and prepare returns HostFailed('egress_oversize') instead of the atomic NeedsGrooming D4 promises.
findings.disposition: Deferred noncritical: reassessment sizing includes the complete Used evidence but still uses the current request_id/revision. A future owner allocating larger fresh identity fields may encounter a later egress_oversize hold at the edge. No oversized request is sent or sufficient result inferred. Reserving all possible future owner identity growth remains a known atomic-enrichment completeness limitation.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:182`: schema_path's segment regex `\.([a-z_]+)` cannot match field names that contain digits (sha256, privacy_sha256, snapshot_sha256, base_candidate_sha256). Errors on those fields fall back to a parent path or to empty, not the longest allowed ancestor D4 specifies.

   Failure scenario: A wire request with "snapshot_sha256": 5 returns Invalid('request','schema','') instead of '/snapshot_sha256'. A type error at $.policy_revision.sha256 reports '/policy_revision', and $.invocation.sha256 reports '/invocation'.
findings.disposition: Addressed: the diagnostic path parser admits digits after the first field-name character, retaining allowed sha256 field paths while dynamic/private key projection remains bounded.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:660`: _request_invalid turns every InvalidHost into code 'invariant', so host-grammar Faults that _host raises as 'schema' (range or regex failures) are misreported by decode_request and egress. This is the remainder of R1 #4.

   Failure scenario: A wire request with "revision": 0, "request_id": "bad id!" or an uppercase policy sha256 passes strict convert. _host then raises Fault('schema','/revision'), prepare returns InvalidHost('/revision'), and decode_request reports Invalid('request','invariant','/revision') instead of schema.
findings.disposition: Deferred noncritical: semantic host grammar Faults still normalize through InvalidHost to invariant rather than schema at the same safe public field path. Invalid input remains refused; no authority or unsafe output results. Diagnostic classification precision remains incomplete.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/validate.py:306`: _origin_fields treats a missing or non-dict permission `invocation` envelope as an origin gap. invocation also carries the host-owned cwd_id/sha256, so this is host envelope corruption, which D4 says must be invalid_host.

   Failure scenario: A permission request with invocation=None returns OriginGap(schema, '/invocation/input'). permission_disposition then gives EscalateProposal('input_profile') and decode_request reports a schema error blaming the origin, instead of EscalateProposal('invalid_host').
findings.disposition: Addressed: absent/non-dict permission invocation is classified as InvalidHost at /invocation before origin input validation. Actual invocation.input remains origin-owned.

findings.finding:
`src/heterodyne/gatekeeper/_rule_identity.py:31`: The fingerprint attests kernel.redact_with_dirs read from the redact module, but validate._text calls its own `redact_with_dirs` binding captured at import, so the function actually doing the redaction is never fingerprinted. Separately, the fingerprint includes docstring constants, so running under python -OO silently fails every privacy context closed.

    Failure scenario: Rebinding heterodyne.gatekeeper.validate.redact_with_dirs leaves rules_match() True while every _text check runs different code. Under `python -OO`, redact_with_dirs' docstring is stripped from co_consts, the fingerprint changes, and every prepare/check_result returns InvalidHost or binding: a total gatekeeper outage that the CPython 3.12 disclosure does not mention.
findings.disposition: Addressed binding; disclosed runtime limit: privacy admission now checks the exact function binding actually called as well as the loaded kernel fingerprint. EXPECTED is unchanged. Only unoptimized CPython 3.12 is admitted; -OO strips fingerprinted docstrings and fails closed, as now explicitly documented. No optimized runtime admission or source-authentication claim is added.
